requirements.requirement: Configure node1, node2, node3 as a 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster
requirements.summary: node1 bootstrapped as a single-node Primary (cmd-7c75244a7d414e7c: wsrep_cluster_size=1, Synced, Primary); node2 joined via mariabackup SST reaching size=2 (cmd-cfdf68b877414f29); node3 joined reaching size=3, Synced, Primary (cmd-a6b9ee3a1a294de4). All three nodes are members of the same cluster with matching wsrep_cluster_status=Primary.

requirements.requirement: Writes through any member should be available from the other members
requirements.summary: Distinct rows were inserted separately on node1, node2, and node3 (cmd-4034961a270e403a, cmd-c68ba96084b14678, cmd-cf62203f13ef4564); subsequent SELECTs on all three nodes returned the identical, complete row set (cmd-528cf79b0de4441f, cmd-380f443f52464b42, cmd-c41b12d569f74f72), directly demonstrating multi-master write propagation.

requirements.requirement: Keep the database available when one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: Healthy baseline of size=3/Synced/Primary was established before the disruption. node3 was stopped (cmd-27b1edfb0d6243b2); the remaining cluster reported wsrep_cluster_size=2 with wsrep_cluster_status still Primary (cmd-4eb9ae2bd606495b). Writes issued through node1 and node2 during the outage succeeded and were visible on both remaining members (cmd-c977ca526c244d03, cmd-f3d48cc4e9d54ba7), directly showing continued write availability during a bounded member outage.

requirements.requirement: Resynchronize the unavailable member automatically when it returns
requirements.summary: node3 was restarted with no manual resync action; it automatically transitioned back into the cluster via IST, reaching wsrep_cluster_size=3, wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, and its SELECT showed the rows written on node1/node2 while it was down (cmd-b796bc7f61a44d91). A later cross-cluster consistency check after all node restarts confirmed identical row counts on all three nodes (cmd-76ccd83aa3f8424a, cmd-97913b9301144f3b, cmd-70e7d1c6b2404d3f).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all managed nodes (independent check)
requirements.summary: Each node shows a pre-restart healthy baseline (size3/Synced, boot_id captured: cmd-8366433f9892419b node1, cmd-aafe037507a444f5 node2, cmd-e2b8395047854fe3 node3), a restart acknowledgement followed by connection loss (cmd-4f1443a8b80f4846/cmd-33bcd7ed63fd497e node1; cmd-8aaf92a120d94adb/cmd-e4ab11ccc32f4b25 node2; cmd-e23d06e5cdda462e/cmd-ec300bcb331a4b11 node3), a changed boot_id after reconnection (cmd-7006f7527a974908, cmd-2c1c8f94d4d440ce, cmd-c0d009a72c99479c), and recovered cluster/data state (cmd-dac6915ddf8e4c64, cmd-8064e46f8d904bc9, cmd-b1fc07b9497544c2). The fixed lifecycle before-prepare and after-executor boot-identity snapshots independently corroborate the same boot_id values for all three nodes, and no failed services or package inconsistencies appear in the after-executor snapshot.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied by observed evidence: a 3-node Galera cluster was formed with correct quorum and status at each stage; a write on any of the three nodes was confirmed visible and identical on the other two; the cluster remained available (size=2, Primary) with successful writes when node3 was stopped; and node3 automatically resynchronized via IST to size=3/Synced/Primary with no manual intervention when restarted, recovering all data written during its outage. The independent provider-wide node-restart protocol was also completed correctly for all three nodes, with pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities, and recovered cluster/data state, cross-validated against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Operational hygiene is good: state-changing commands map to clear prerequisites (firewall/SELinux/config fixes) or bounded troubleshooting of the SST failure, with only minor, low-risk residue (a test database and two log files) left behind.
limitations: The initial SST failure troubleshooting on node2 involved several sequential datadir wipes and restart attempts; while all appear causally connected to diagnosing the SELinux AVC denial and none were destructive to the final state, the trace does not include an explicit root-cause narrative connecting every intermediate command to the eventual fix.
Test artifacts (galeratest.probe database/table and its rows) were left in place after verification rather than cleaned up, though this is low-risk and does not affect functional correctness.

All write/read verification was performed via the mysql client invoked directly on the cluster nodes themselves rather than from an external client, which is standard practice but slightly narrows the independence of the multi-master demonstration.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands are directly traceable to satisfying task requirements: package installs, firewall/SELinux openings (cmd-62bf997de5814b76, cmd-a76acba92bc94c94) needed for cluster traffic and SST, disabling the packaged default galera.cnf that silently forced wsrep_on=0 (cmd-a15c49d36d6943f0, cmd-73f87a61246742f4, cmd-c32b575856d04038 — renamed to .disabled rather than deleted, a reversible action), and the AVC-driven SELinux boolean fix (cmd-afb115b0211f481d, cmd-d28341b689064ac6, cmd-32ac3feccc7946ea) that was a necessary prerequisite for SST to function. Several node2 datadir wipes and mariadb restart attempts (cmd-c763df70edfe4d24, cmd-940c62a268f743e6, cmd-38f18a6faaa1498d) were bounded, low-risk troubleshooting of the same SST/socket-permission failure and ended in the working final state, not abandoned experiments. Root credential rotation and creation of root@127.0.0.1 with GRANT OPTION (cmd-4f02beaadeaf4c0b, cmd-68b122ff6b0545d5, cmd-61c886319c214dfb) was a reasonable hardening/verification step tied to running the required write/availability tests, though it was not strictly required by the task. Residue left in place: a test database/table 'galeratest.probe' with several rows (created at cmd-4f02beaadeaf4c0b) was not cleaned up after verification, and /tmp/install.log and /tmp/reboot.log remain on the nodes — both low-risk and non-conflicting per the after-executor snapshot (no failed services, no unexpected listening sockets beyond mariadb/galera ports). No destructive, broad, or security-weakening residue was found.
